issues.description: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None; caller will happily build a garbage URL with 'None' in the path
issues.detail: If the regex doesn't match, the function returns None and use_koji_url_only concatenates it straight into the path: '/latest/None/Packages/...'. No check, no raise, no log. The patch will produce a broken URL and the failure will surface much later at fetch time with a useless 404. Either raise an exception with the offending URL in the message, or assert. Don't quietly emit None.

issues.description: nevra is extracted by basename split but treated as a NEVRA string; if the filename has no .rpm or includes query params it breaks
issues.detail: url.split('/')[-1] gives whatever the last path segment is. The koji canonical path is '<first-letter-of-name>/<full-rpm-filename>', so nevra[0].lower() taking the first character of the filename happens to work for normal 'name-version-release.arch.rpm' filenames but breaks the moment the URL has a query string, a fragment, or anything other than a bare .rpm. There's no validation that this is actually an RPM filename. Add a sanity check (endswith('.rpm')) and fail loud if not.

issues.description: 'coreos-pool' substring match is too loose for the koji_url_base check
issues.detail: The check 'if koji_url_base in url' is fine, but the older code at line 165 uses 'if "coreos-pool" in url' which is a bare substring. If anyone ever names a repo 'not-coreos-pool-mirror' it matches. Not introduced by this patch, but worth noting since this patch is now doubling down on the coreos-pool naming. A constant at module level would be better than two different string literals in two functions.

issues.description: arch list is hardcoded in two places in the codebase now
issues.detail: The arches ['x86_64', 'aarch64', 'ppc64le', 's390x'] are hardcoded inside extract_arch_from_url. If the project already has a canonical arch list (it does — get_basearch is imported from cosalib.cmdlib), this should reference that or a shared constant. Otherwise the next arch addition is a two-place edit waiting to be forgotten.

issues.description: commit message acknowledges race condition and untestability but ships anyway with no mitigation hook
issues.detail: The author honestly flags two real downsides: race between koji tag and Konflux build, and inability to test rpms.lock.yaml changes locally. Fine, the tradeoff may be acceptable for Konflux-only consumption, but there's no retry, no verification step, no comment in the code pointing future maintainers at the race. Six-months-from-now-maintainer hits a flaky Konflux build and has zero breadcrumb. At minimum, leave a comment at the use_koji_url_only call site referencing the race and the koji-tagger dependency.

issues.description: no tests added for the new URL-rewriting function
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only and extract_arch_from_url are pure string-manipulation functions. They are the easiest thing in the world to unit test. There are no tests in this diff. Given the project has cases the author is explicitly trying to handle (fedora-secondary URLs for ppc64le and s390x), a handful of input/output examples as tests would protect the next person who touches this. Pure functions with no tests is unforced sloppiness.

review.summary: The patch solves a real DNF5 bug with a reasonable workaround: rewrite all non-coreos-pool URLs to the canonical koji path, relying on coreos-koji-tagger to make the URL valid after merge. The shape is fine and the diff is scoped. What's wrong is the failure mode: extract_arch_from_url returns None on miss and the caller cheerfully builds a broken URL with 'None' in the path; the NEVRA extraction is naive basename-splitting with no .rpm sanity check; the arch list is hardcoded in a file that already imports get_basearch from a shared lib; and there are zero unit tests for two pure functions that are trivially testable. The race condition and local-untestability are honestly documented in the commit but not breadcrumbed in the code. NEEDS-WORK: add validation that fails loud instead of producing garbage URLs, share the arch list, and write the obvious tests.
